gen.title: Locus specificity and human pairing patterns

cards.stem: How is random mating described for the genetic region under study
options: arbitrary with regard to the locus
cards.quote: Random mating implies that mating should be arbitrary with regard to the locus being considered.
cards.hint: Focus on how choice should relate to the gene region considered

cards.stem: Which genotype frequency change follows when similar individuals tend to pair
cards.quote: Positive assortative mating leads to an increase in homozygotes whereas negative assortative mating leads to an increase in heterozygotes.
cards.hint: Think about what similar pairing does to identical allele pairs

cards.stem: How is the rarer dissimilar pairing form defined in the text
options: breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes
cards.quote: In contrast, negative assortative mating is breeding between individuals with dissimilar genotypes, and is more rare.
cards.hint: Look for the definition that mentions dissimilar genotypes

cards.stem: For which trait do people still pair without preference despite other preferences
cards.quote: they mate randomly with respect to other traits such as blood type and short tandem repeat (STR) genotype.
cards.hint: Consider traits unrelated to visible characteristics where pairing is unbiased
